title: Document Archive Index
dataSources: Tree records (`genealogy:record`), DNA matches (`dna:match`), ancestor events (`ancestor:event`), archive documents (`archive:document`), tree nodes (`familytree:node`).
app: Genealogy and family-history research — tree platforms (Ancestry, FamilySearch), DNA match exports (23andMe, MyHeritage), and document / archive catalogues — streamed to Splunk HEC via GEDCOM and CSV exports.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=archive:document
| stats count as docs, sum(eval(if(transcribed="yes",1,0))) as transcribed by doc_type
| eval to_do=docs-transcribed
| sort - to_do
description: Catalogues your scanned certificates, letters, and photos by type and flags how many still need transcribing.
value: A searchable archive index means precious documents are findable and the transcription backlog is visible.
implementation: Ingest document metadata into `index=personal`; summarise by type and transcription status.
visualization: Bar chart of documents by type and transcription status.
grandmaExplanation: It sorts your family documents by kind and shows which still need typing up, so nothing precious is lost.
